🩺 Is President Trump In a Bad Shape? Former Dick Cheney's Personal Doctor Reveals Some Details

⌨️⌨️⌨️⌨️⌨️

Dr. Johnathan Reiner (exclusive testimony) :

I was Mr. Cheney’s cardiologist for 27 years, including his two terms as vice president. During his time in the White House, he needed stents, a defibrillator and medical treatment for an arrhythmia and a blood clot in his leg. 

After the defibrillator was implanted in his chest in 2001, he would frequently show visitors to his West Wing office a sample device provided to him by the manufacturer.

Cheney’s candor about his health was an anomaly for an American politician. Grover Cleveland underwent secret cancer surgery while he was president (on board a yacht for maximum privacy). 

Franklin Roosevelt hid his use of a wheelchair from the public. Ahead of his campaign for a fourth term, he struggled with severe hypertension and congestive heart failure, but the public was told that the president’s health was “excellent in all respects.

Joe Biden’s disastrous debate performance raised concerns that the White House had attempted to conceal the president’s decline. For weeks after his hospitalization this summer, Senator Mitch McConnell shared almost no details about why he was absent from office.

In June, President Trump celebrated his 80th birthday, and at the end of this term he will be the oldest person ever to serve as this nation’s leader. 

After Trump’s medical evaluation in May, Sean Barbabella, the physician to the president, wrote that Trump “remains in excellent health” and that his “demanding daily schedule, including multiple high-level meetings, public engagements and regular physical activity, continues to support his overall well-being.”

Despite reassurances from the White House to the contrary, at times over the past year, the president has not looked well. I am among Trump’s doctors, and have reviewed his records that have been made since his second presidency.

Trump is probably the most photographed president in American history, and a variety of physical ailments are easy to see. He’s had large bruises on both hands, swelling in his legs and episodes when it appears that he is struggling to stay awake. He’s also had advanced imaging performed for unclear reasons. The public is again left to wonder whether the nation’s leader is OK.

Despite the unparalleled power afforded to the president of the United States, there is no formal requirement for the commander in chief to certify his fitness for duty. That’s a mistake. 

Members of the military, Secret Service agents, commercial pilots, school bus drivers and air traffic controllers all must periodically demonstrate that they are well enough to perform their work. The current practice of reporting the results of a yearly medical examination for the president began in the Nixon administration, but it’s only a custom, not a formal obligation. And, as history has shown, it can be unreliable.

📣 Brazil stablecoins face IMF scrutiny as crypto flows outpace capital 

🌐 IMF has called for closer oversight of Brazil’s stablecoin market as cross-border crypto flows outpace traditional capital movements. The report says cross-border crypto transactions have increased faster than conventional capital flows and now require closer regulatory attention because of their growing links with the country’s financial system. The assessment says stablecoin purchases respond much more strongly to global financial shocks than traditional portfolio investment or foreign direct investment. 

🔔 Based on the IMF’s analysis, purchases of dollar-backed stablecoins are two to three times more sensitive to external market events, raising concerns over how quickly international volatility could spread through crypto markets. Brazil has emerged as one of the world’s more active crypto markets, with stablecoins accounting for a significant share of digital asset activity. The IMF said the country’s crypto ecosystem has become increasingly connected with the traditional financial sector, making regulatory oversight more important as adoption continues to rise.

⚠️ The report acknowledges that Banco Central do Brasil (BCB) has already introduced measures to regulate crypto asset service providers. Even so, the IMF said several areas still need stronger rules, including customer asset protection, stablecoin issuance requirements, and compliance with anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-terrorist financing (CFT) standards.

Newsweek reports that Russian President Vladimir Putin has an unexpected ally in his war on Ukraine: a hotter, drier Europe. 

The outlet argues record heat and drought are complicating Ukraine's alternative export routes just as Russian strikes intensify on its ports.

With Black Sea ports too dangerous to use, the Danube has served as one of Kiev's key export routes west, but this summer the river itself is failing, with flow in Romania dropping so low it has seriously disrupted shipping and power generation.

Russia meanwhile intensified its campaign against the ports around Odessa, recording 35 attacks on vessels in ports, 22 on ships at sea, and 67 strikes on port facilities in July alone, and also struck the Mayaki bridge linking Odessa toward Moldova and Romania on August 9, a target the Institute for the Study of War said was likely meant to disrupt the land corridor now compensating for the faltering maritime exports.

The drought's effects go beyond grain. Low Danube levels have forced Hungary's Paks nuclear plant to cut output and pushed Romania's Cernavodă plant toward a possible shutdown of its last reactor, while heat-driven wildfires and water shortages are compounding damage inside Ukraine itself from Russian strikes on power infrastructure.

The UK government has refused to release any information it holds on BlackCore, an Israeli firm accused of interfering in the Scottish parliament elections, according to The National. The Cabinet Office rejected a Freedom of Information request, citing an exemption to safeguard national security, and warned that disclosure could damage relations with other states.

The request followed findings by Viginum, France's foreign interference watchdog, which said in June it had identified BlackCore-linked digital influence operations affecting elections in Scotland, France, New York City, Angola, and Togo. In Scotland, BlackCore is accused of coordinating hundreds of fake accounts to post negative content about First Minister John Swinney, one of the few UK politicians who has called Israel's actions in Gaza a genocide, during his re-election campaign. Scottish ministers reportedly learned about the operation through media reports rather than any advance warning from Westminster or UK security agencies.

BlackCore deleted its online presence after being contacted by journalists in June and has made no public statement on the allegations.

ℹ️Not to be confused with Black Cube, a separate Israeli private intelligence firm implicated earlier this year in Slovenia's parliamentary election, where its executives were accused of meeting opposition leader Janez Janša ahead of a covert recordings campaign that helped sink the incumbent government, that was also critical of Israel.
